messages:
sarah.ops: Heads-up — we need a short rolling maintenance window tomorrow 03:00-06:00 UTC to upgrade the GPU driver and the NIC kernel module on eu-west3 racks. This is to fix intermittent p99 stalls we've seen during KV-cache heavy workloads.
ben.eng: how many racks/nodes are in scope?
sarah.ops: ~18 racks, ~540 GPUs total. We'll do cohorted drains (6 racks at a time) with staggered reboots and KV cache warm-seeding on the target pools. Expect ~3-6% transient capacity dip per cohort.
priya.se: Dedicated customers — please confirm we send 72h notice + opt-in blackout window option. Private deployments (VPC) not impacted.
sarah.ops: yes on 72h notice. We'll email enterprise contacts and post to status with the optional blackout link.
henry.oncall: Can we run a canary in the morning for the node agent + nic driver on 2 racks before the full window? Prefer 01:30 UTC canary so we catch any immediate regressions.
sarah.ops: good call. Canary scheduled 01:30-02:00 UTC in az-eu-west3-cohort-a (2 racks). If canary fails, we abort full run and roll back.
alex.sre: adding runbook snippet for coordinator and ops to follow during drains:
```
# cordon + drain sequence (example)
for node in $(list-cohort nodes); do
  kubectl cordon $node
  kubectl drain $node --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='service!=platform-monitor'
  ssh $node sudo systemctl stop model-server
  ssh $node sudo apt-get install -y gpu-driver-57 nic-kmod-1.2.3
  reboot $node
  wait-for-health $node --checks model-serving,kv-cache-ready,net-e2e
done
```
alex.sre: After reboot, run kv-seed: `redwood-kv-seed --pool=gradient --parallel=8` and confirm 95th-latency back to baseline.
ben.eng: what's the fallback plan if KV seed is slow and backfills are causing higher cost?
sarah.ops: fallback = stop seeding, bring next cohort online and extend canary window. Also have rollback image available (gpu-driver-56 + nic-kmod-1.2.1). Cost note: full run could add ~$6-8k in transient GPU-hours for cache backfills, estimate in ticket.
priya.se: I'll prepare the customer comms draft and opt-out link. Also flagging that some enterprise tenants requested maintenance during business hours — we've accepted two requests and moved their tenants to later cohorts.
henry.oncall: telemetry to watch during the run: p99 token latency, model-server OOMs, NIC rx_err, pod eviction rate. I’ll leave alerts muted for noisy transient evictions but with paging thresholds higher by 2x for the window.
ops-bot: Runbook page updated -> https://internal.redwood/runbooks/infra/eu-west3-driver-upgrade (edited) :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled at 1714055400 for cohort-a (automated rollback 1714057200)
sarah.ops: please react with :thumbsup: once you've read and are OK with the schedule. I'll cut the status post and the 72h customer email after final signoff.
alex.sre: OK from SRE side. I'll own run coordination and rollback path.
ben.eng: OK from Eng. I'll monitor serving metrics and flamegraph any p99 spikes.
priya.se: OK for comms. Will publish draft in #announcements for review.
henry.oncall: I'll be on shift for the window and will escalate if canary >10% regressions.
sarah.ops: thanks everyone. final note — keep the cohort order flexible: we prioritize racks with spare capacity first to reduce blast radius.
